result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely obstructed by a large vehicle parked across the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the travel lane. The street lacks basic safety features like marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or buffers, and is characterized by industrial land use with blank frontages.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstruction
hazards.description: A large red tow truck is parked completely across the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction
hazards.description: The parked truck and the corner of the industrial building create significant blind spots for pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Bollards
interventions.description: Install physical barriers such as bollards along the curb line to prevent vehicles from parking on and obstructing the pedestrian walkway.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks to provide designated and safer crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions to reduce crossing distances and improve sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a basic sidewalk separated from a parking lot by a chain-link fence, but it lacks a buffer from the roadway. The street is wide and lacks lane markings or designated pedestrian crossings, which may encourage higher vehicle speeds and create a hostile environment for crossing.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide street can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The large tree and parked vehicles can obscure pedestrians attempting to enter the roadway from the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground (tree) and along the right curb (parked car)

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to designate safe crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Lane Striping
interventions.description: Add clear lane markings to organize traffic flow and potentially narrow travel lanes to reduce vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, characterized by a lack of continuous sidewalks and a massive, undefined vehicle entrance that forces pedestrians into the roadway. There is no separation between people and vehicles in the foreground, and the infrastructure for safe crossing is entirely absent.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no paved walkway for pedestrians in the foreground, forcing them to walk in the vehicle travel area.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire foreground and right side of the image

hazards.name: Excessive Curb Cut Width
hazards.description: The entrance to the parking lot is extremely wide and undefined, creating a large conflict zone between pedestrians and turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the asphalt opens into the lot

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and utility poles block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers at the edge of the parking area.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a raised, ADA-compliant sidewalk through the entire block to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the vehicle entrance to the minimum necessary and clearly define it with a continuous sidewalk and curb to slow turning traffic.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Install street trees and a buffer zone to separate the new sidewalk from the roadway and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The environment is extremely hostile to pedestrians, characterized by a complete lack of dedicated walkways or crossing infrastructure. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with heavy vehicles in an industrial setting where sightlines are severely obstructed by parked trucks.

hazards.name: Absence of Pedestrian Walkways
hazards.description: There are no sidewalks, forcing pedestrians to walk directly in the path of vehicle traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible area

hazards.name: Severe Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large commercial vehicles and trucks parked along the roadway block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the street where trucks are parked

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: The pavement is cracked and uneven, creating trip hazards for anyone walking in the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install raised, paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide physical separation from vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Parking Management
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections and potential crossing points to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Marked Pedestrian Crossings
interventions.description: Add high-visibility crosswalks to designate safe areas for pedestrians to cross the industrial corridor.
